# Express app updates for Auth0 admin features (2025-12-13 00:28Z)

_**User (2025-12-13 00:36Z)**_

You are working inside this repo: https://github.com/saisenee/ReVamp

It is an Express app serving static HTML/CSS/JS from /public and private pages in /private, using express-openid-connect (Auth0). Do not migrate frameworks (no React/Next). Keep the current structure.

Use this Repomix file as the full source of truth for the codebase. Before coding, make a step-by-step plan and list files you will change.

Goals

Landing page UI

Update /public/index.html and /public/style.css to match my wireframe layout.

I can provide a background image later, so for now add a placeholder and structure the layout so swapping the image is easy.

Auth0 login status on top right

Keep login/logout working.

In the header top-right, show: profile picture + name (or “Guest”) + Login/Logout button.

If logged in and user is authorized as admin, also show an “Admin” link/button.

Admin authorization

Only an authorized “Business owner” (admin) can:

Edit business title

Edit products

Delete products

There should be:

A public page that anyone can view

An admin page that only admins can access

Implementation requirement: Use Auth0-based authorization. Prefer Auth0 RBAC roles/permissions (e.g., admin) if possible; otherwise use a short-term allowlist (like emails) via env vars for development.

Data + routes

Create CRUD endpoints for products and business title.

Public endpoints allow read-only access.

Admin endpoints require authentication + admin authorization.

Deliverables

A clear implementation plan first.

Then code changes with short explanations.

Call out any new environment variables needed (update .env.example).

Keep the UI simple but clean.

Start by analyzing the repomix and identifying the best place to add:

admin checks (middleware)

admin routes (e.g., /admin, /api/admin/...)

product storage (in-memory to start is fine, but isolate it so we can replace with DB later)This file is a merged representation of the entire codebase, combined into a single document by Repomix.

## File: public/script.js
````javascript
 1: const isLandingPage = document.getElementById('landing') ? true : false
 2: const isVaultPage = document.getElementById('vault') ? true : false
 3: 
 4: const response = await fetch('/api/user')
 5: const data = await response.json()
 6: 
 7: const isAuthenticated = data.isAuthenticated
 8: const displayName = data.name || 'Guest'
 9: const displayEmail = data.email || 'Welcome'
10: const profilePicture = data.picture || 'user.svg'
11: 
12: const authButton = isAuthenticated
13:     ? '<a class="button" href="/logout">Logout</a>'
14:     : '<a class="button" href="/login">Login</a>'
15: 
16: const vaultLink = isAuthenticated && isLandingPage
17:     ? '<a class="button" href="/vault">Enter Vault</a>'
18:     : ''
19: 
20: profile.innerHTML = `
21:         <img src="${profilePicture}" onerror="this.onerror=null;this.src='user.svg';">
22:         <div>
23:             <h4>${displayName}</h4>
24:             <h5>${displayEmail}</h5>
25:         </div>
26:         ${authButton}
27:         ${vaultLink}
28:     `
29: 
30: if (isLandingPage && content) {
31:     content.innerHTML = isAuthenticated
32:         ? `<span class="secret-sauce">
33:                     Your <a href="/vault">secret sauce</a> is ready.
34:                </span>`
35:         : `<span class="secret-sauce">
36:                     Have you tried our <a href="/vault">secret sauce</a>?
37:                </span>`
38: }
39: 
40: if (isAuthenticated && isVaultPage) {
41:     // the vault endpoint only works for logged in users
42:     // see also, the /api/secrets endpoint in ./server.js
43:     try {
44:         const response = await fetch('/api/secrets')
45:         const data = await response.json()
46:         const vaultHTML = `<span class="secret-sauce">
47:             Here you go.
48:             </span>
49:             <ul class="items">
50:                 ${data.map(item =>
51:             `<li>
52:                     <a class="sauce" target="_blank" href="${item.url}">
53:                         <span>${item.name}</span>
54:                     </a>
55:                 </li>`)
56:                 .join('')}
57:             </ul>`;
58: 
59:         content.innerHTML = DOMPurify.sanitize(vaultHTML)
60:     }
61:     catch (e) {
62:         console.log(e)
63:     }
64: }
65: 
66: if (logo) {
67:     logo.addEventListener('click', () => {
68:         window.location.href = '/'
69:     })
70: }
````

## File: README.md
````markdown
 1: # Vault  
 2: This is an example of an [Express](https://expressjs.com) app that uses [Auth0](https://auth0.com/) for User authentication. It displays a public landing page, but also shares secret data via an `/api/secrets` endpoint. This makes use of `isAuthenticated` logic to ensure the user is logged in before sending the secret data.
 3: 
 4: ## Setup Auth0
 5: To use this code, create your own [Auth0](https://auth0.com/) account.
 6: - In the Auth0 dashboard choose `Create Application` 
 7: - Choose the `Regular Web Application` option 
 8: - When asked "What technology are you using", choose `Express`.
 9: - Select `Integrate Now` to Configure Auth0 with these settings:
10: - Allowed Callback URL: `http://localhost:3000/callback`
11: - Allowed Logout URLs: `http://localhost:3000`
12: 
13: ## Integrate Auth0 
14: The Auth0 quickstart includes an `Integrate the SDK` section. This is useful as a point of comparison; this repo is setup in a similar way, but we will use Environment Variables, instead of hard-coding the details. These variables to the parameters that are needed by the Auth0 router, as specified in the [Auth0 documentation](https://auth0.com/docs/quickstart/webapp/express/interactive).  
15: 
16: ### Setup Environment Variables
17: Here's an example `.env` file showing the environment variables that are needed. You'll find something similar in the `.env.example` file included with in this repo.  *You will need to modify them* to fit your own Auth0 account details.  
18: 
19: ```
20: BASE_URL=http://localhost:3000              # URL where the application is served 
21: SECRET=*****                                # A long, random string
22: CLIENT_ID=*****                             # Client ID found in your Application settings
23: ISSUER_BASE_URL=https://*****.auth0.com     # Auth0 URL found in your Application settings
24: ```
25: 
26: ## Deploying to Vercel
27: When deploying to Vercel:
28: 1. Add the above settings as [Environment Variables](https://vercel.com/docs/environment-variables) to your Vercel project during deployment, (or via Project > Settings > Environment Variables). *Important:* For the `BASE_URL`, use your actual Vercel project URL (e.g. `https://my-project.vercel.app`), instead of `localhost`. 
29: 2. Update your Auth0 dashboard settings to allow Vercel:
30: -Allowed Callback URL: `http://localhost:3000/callback,https://my-project.vercel.app/callback`
31: -Allowed Logout URLs: `http://localhost:3000,https://my-project.vercel.app`
32: 
33: ## Note
34: If you're publishing templates via Express, you can also use the [requiresAuth](https://auth0.github.io/express-openid-connect/functions/requiresAuth.html) middleware that ships with Express OpenID Connect. This would allow you to automatically redirect users to a login page when they attempt to reach a secured page.

p.id === id);\n    if (index === -1) return null;\n    \n    const product = store.products[index];\n    if (data.name !== undefined) product.name = data.name;\n    if (data.description !== undefined) product.description = data.description;\n    if (data.price !== undefined) product.price = parseFloat(data.price);\n    if (data.image !== undefined) product.image = data.image;\n    \n    return { ...product };\n}\n\nexport function deleteProduct(id) {\n    const index = store.products.findIndex(p =&gt; p.id === id);\n    if (index === -1) return false;\n    store.products.splice(index, 1);\n    return true;\n}\n\nexport default {\n    getBusiness,\n    updateBusiness,\n    getProducts,\n    getProductById,\n    createProduct,\n    updateProduct,\n    deleteProduct\n};\n",

  "textEditContent": "// Auth middleware for admin authorization\n// Supports Auth0 RBAC roles OR email allowlist (via ADMIN_EMAILS env var)\n\n/**\n * Check if user has admin role via Auth0 RBAC\n * Requires Auth0 to be configured with roles and the \"roles\" claim in the ID token\n */\nfunction hasAdminRole(user) {\n    // Auth0 RBAC: roles are typically in a custom namespace claim\n    // e.g., \"https://myapp.com/roles\" or just \"roles\" depending on Auth0 config\n    const roles = user?.['https://revamp.app/roles'] \n                || user?.roles \n                || user?.['http://schemas.microsoft.com/ws/2008/06/identity/claims/role']\n                || [];\n    return Array.isArray(roles) &amp;&amp; roles.includes('admin');\n}\n\n/**\n * Check if user email is in the admin allowlist (for development)\n */\nfunction isEmailAllowlisted(user) {\n    const adminEmails = process.env.ADMIN_EMAILS;\n    if (!adminEmails) return false;\n    \n    const allowlist = adminEmails.split(',').map(e =&gt; e.trim().toLowerCase());\n    const userEmail = user?.email?.toLowerCase();\n    return userEmail &amp;&amp; allowlist.includes(userEmail);\n}\n\n/**\n * Determine if the current user is an admin\n * @param {object} user - The Auth0 user object from req.oidc.user\n * @returns {boolean}\n */\nexport function isAdmin(user) {\n    if (!user) return false;\n    return hasAdminRole(user) || isEmailAllowlisted(user);\n}\n\n/**\n * Middleware: Requires the user to be authenticated\n */\nexport function requireAuth(req, res, next) {\n    if (!req.oidc?.isAuthenticated()) {\n        return res.status(401).json({ error: 'Authentication required' });\n    }\n    next();\n}\n\n/**\n * Middleware: Requires the user to be an authenticated admin\n */\nexport function requireAdmin(req, res, next) {\n    if (!req.oidc?.isAuthenticated()) {\n        return res.status(401).json({ error: 'Authentication required' });\n    }\n    if (!isAdmin(req.oidc.user)) {\n        return res.status(403).json({ error: 'Admin access required' });\n    }\n    next();\n}\n\n/**\n * Middleware for HTML pages: Redirects to login if not authenticated,\n * then shows 403 page if not admin\n */\nexport function requireAdminPage(req, res, next) {\n    if (!req.oidc?.isAuthenticated()) {\n        return res.redirect('/login');\n    }\n    if (!isAdmin(req.oidc.user)) {\n        return res.status(403).send(&#96;\n            &lt;!DOCTYPE html&gt;\n            &lt;html&gt;\n            &lt;head&gt;&lt;title&gt;Access Denied&lt;/title&gt;&lt;/head&gt;\n            &lt;body style=\"font-family: sans-serif; text-align: center; padding: 4rem;\"&gt;\n                &lt;h1&gt;403 - Access Denied&lt;/h1&gt;\n                &lt;p&gt;You do not have admin privileges.&lt;/p&gt;\n                &lt;a href=\"/\"&gt;Return Home&lt;/a&gt;\n            &lt;/body&gt;\n            &lt;/html&gt;\n        &#96;);\n    }\n    next();\n}\n\nexport default {\n    isAdmin,\n    requireAuth,\n    requireAdmin,\n    requireAdminPage\n};\n",

}

Now let me update `public.html` to include the auth header: Now let me check the end of `public.html` to update the script section: Now let me update `admin.html` to add auth checks and the header: Now let me check and update the end of `admin.html` to add the admin-specific JS: Now let me add the CSS styles for the landing page and auth components: Now I'll add the landing page and auth styles at the end of the CSS file: Now let me update .env.example: Now let me create a default avatar SVG for users without profile pictures: Actually, let me create a proper SVG instead since a blank file won't work: Let me update the HTML files to use the SVG instead: Let me verify the changes don't have any errors: Let me also delete the empty PNG file I accidentally created: Now let me verify everything is in place by checking the key files: Everything looks good! Let me provide a summary of all the changes made.

---

## Summary of Implementation

### Files Created

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `auth.js` | Admin authorization middleware supporting Auth0 RBAC roles and email allowlist fallback |
| `store.js` | In-memory data store for business settings (isolated for future DB migration) |
| `default-avatar.svg` | Default avatar for users without profile pictures |

### Files Modified

| File | Changes |
|------|---------|
| `server.js` | Added admin middleware imports, protected `/admin` and `admin.html` routes with `requireAdminPage`, attached `isAdmin` flag to requests |
| `api.js` | Added `isAdmin` to `/api/user` response, added business settings endpoints (`GET/PUT /api/business`), added admin product routes (`/api/admin/products/:id`) |
| `index.html` | Complete rewrite as landing page with hero section, auth header (profile pic + name + Login/Logout + Admin link), background placeholder |
| `public.html` | Updated nav with auth section showing user profile/name and Admin link for admins, dynamically loads business title |
| `admin.html` | Added sidebar user profile, Shop Settings panel for editing business title, client-side admin verification |
| `revamp-style.css` | Added ~300 lines of landing page, auth header, admin sidebar, and shop settings styles |
| `.env.example` | Added `ADMIN_EMAILS` environment variable |

### New Environment Variables

```env
# Admin Authorization - comma-separated list of admin email addresses
# Fallback for when Auth0 RBAC is not configured
ADMIN_EMAILS=admin@example.com,owner@yourbusiness.com
```

### API Endpoints

| Endpoint | Auth | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| `GET /api/user` | Public | Returns user info with `isAdmin` flag |
| `GET /api/business` | Public | Get business title/description |
| `PUT /api/business` | Admin | Update business title/description |
| `PUT /api/admin/products/:id` | Admin | Admin can edit any product |
| `DELETE /api/admin/products/:id` | Admin | Admin can delete any product |

### Authorization Flow

1. **Auth0 RBAC (preferred)**: Checks for `admin` role in Auth0 token claims
2. **Email Allowlist (fallback)**: Checks if user's email is in `ADMIN_EMAILS` env var

### To swap the hero background image

Replace `/img/hero-bg.jpg` with your image, or edit the `.hero-background` style in `undefined`:

```html
<div class="hero-background" style="background-image: url('/img/your-image.jpg');">
```
